3: Compared to human reviewers, GPT-4 feedback on 308 AI and computational biology researchers' own research reports was rated more helpful than at least some human reviewers' feedback by 82.4% of those researchers.
4: Poe Assistant, GPT 3.5, and Google Bard drafting IRB standard operating procedures (SOPs) on 16 topics covered the key sections of reference SOPs from Mayo Clinic and Harvard Longwood, but differed in content on 7 of 16 topics.
7: Google Bard, GPT 3.5, Claude-Instant-100k, and GPT 4, single-prompted on 7 health research ethics case studies, answered every case, but all four missed the flawed non-randomized design (case 4) and the eligibility issues (cases 1, 3).
8: Bard, GPT 3.5, Claude-Instant-100k, and GPT 4 writing informed consent documents for 7 health research ethics cases included all fundamental HHS checklist elements, yet all used jargon and none stated how many participants would be recruited.
9: Compared to GPT 3.5 and GPT-4 with in-context learning, the bespoke fine-tuned model MultiVerS (top-20 retrieved evidence) classified the accuracy of held-out citations to 100 biomedical research reports best (micro-F1 score = 0.59).
10: GPT 3.5 with chain-of-thought prompting checking 20 orthodontic systematic review abstracts against 12 items of the reporting guideline PRISMA did not differ significantly from two human raters on 11 items (Fisher's exact test p > 0.05).
11: GPT 3.5 with chain-of-thought prompting checking 20 orthodontic RCT abstracts against 17 items of the reporting guideline CONSORT-A did not differ significantly from two human raters on 15 items (Fisher's exact test p > 0.05).
12: Compared to two clinician reviewers, GPT 3.5 zero-shot scoring 30 implant-dentistry RCT abstracts with the reporting guideline CONSORT-A differed on overall compliance score by 4.9 percentage points on average (Bland-Altman mean difference).
15: Claude 3.7 Sonnet zero-shot checking 245 withdrawn arXiv research reports as PDFs flagged the error behind the withdrawal in only 16.3% of papers within five flagged problems, half its rate when given LaTeX source (33.1%).
16: Compared to GPT-4 (20.7%) and four other LLMs, Claude Opus zero-shot flagging deficient segments in 380 human peer reviews of 100 ICLR research reports on the AAAR-1.0 benchmark was best, but poor (F1 score = 22%).
17: Combining nine runs of Claude 3 Opus, Claude 2, GPT-4, GPT 3.5, and Mixtral-8x22B on 112 pediatric surgery systematic reviews with the reporting guideline PRISMA agreed more with humans as more ratings were deferred (Cohen's kappa = 0.59-0.77).
18: GPT-4o-mini zero-shot checking 21,041 open-access RCT research reports for alignment with the reporting guideline CONSORT found compliance varied by discipline, from 35.2% of items in pharmacology to 63.4% in urology-nephrology.
19: Fine-tuned on GPT-4 Turbo's correct answers, Llama 2 70B checking held-out text of research reports against 8 items of the reporting guideline CONSORT beat its zero-shot base model (F1 score = 0.84 vs. 0.63; GPT-4 Turbo on 9 items = 0.89).
21: Compared to human reviewers, the bespoke reviewer agent GAR (GPT-4o-mini) reviewing 200 ICLR 2023 research reports was preferred more often by a GPT-4o judge in pairwise comparisons (Bradley-Terry score: GAR = 0.68 vs. humans = 0.52).
22: Compared to AI-Scientist, AI-Review, ReviewerGPT, and OpenReviewer, the bespoke reviewer agent GAR (GPT-4o-mini) reviewing 3,000 NeurIPS and ICLR research reports was rated most human-like by an LLM judge (3.9-4.0 vs. 2.4-3.4 of 5).
23: Compared to AI-Scientist (F1 score = 0.57), the bespoke reviewer agent GAR (GPT-4o-mini) predicting acceptance of 1,000 ICLR 2022 research reports did best (F1 score = 0.66), above humans in a separate NeurIPS consistency study (0.49).
24: Compared to five other LLMs with RAG, GPT 3.5-turbo answering 15 questions from the reporting guideline STROBE about 39 observational medical research reports was most accurate (66.9% vs. GPT 4-1106 = 65.6%, p = .061, to 44.1%).
26: GPT 3.5 few-shot predicting aspect scores from 427 human reviews of ICLR 2017 research reports correlated with human-annotated scores (Pearson's r = 0.65 vs. most-frequent-score baseline = 0.33), but far less given only the paper (r ≤ 0.26).
27: GPT 3.5-turbo zero-shot checking 250 statement-reference pairs from multidisciplinary research reports for quotation errors was most accurate given the cited paper's title and PDF (accuracy = 68%), least given title, abstract, and excerpts (54%).
30: GPT-4 few-shot classifying held-out citations in biomedical research reports for accuracy recognized accurate citations well (F1 score = 0.80) but rarely caught inaccurate ones (F1 score = 0.09 vs. fine-tuned MultiVerS = 0.43).
36: GPT-4 answering 196 multiple-choice questions built from reviews of 14 ICLR 2023 Computer Science research reports on the novel RR-MCQ benchmark got only 28% fully right (exact-match accuracy; GPT 3.5 = 13%).
37: GPT-4 Turbo zero-shot checking 250 statement-reference pairs from multidisciplinary research reports for quotation errors was best given the reference's title, abstract, and excerpts (accuracy = 70%), above GPT-4o and GPT 3.5-turbo (68%).
38: GPT-4 Turbo zero-shot checking a held-out 20% of text from 113 sports medicine RCT research reports against 9 items of the reporting guideline CONSORT matched a systematic review's labels (F1 score = 0.89; items = 0.57-1.00).
39: Five expert evaluators comparing reviews of 150 ICLR, NeurIPS, and Nature research reports preferred GPT-4 Turbo's over human OpenReview reviewers', Command R+, Claude 3 Opus, and Gemini Pro (Bradley-Terry score = 0.56 vs. humans = 0.50).
40: GPT-4 Vision zero-shot checking 20 figures from clinical trial research reports against the reporting guideline CONSORT recognized every participant flow diagram (F1 score = 1.0) but often missed absent dropout reasons (F1 score = 0.58).
41: GPT-4o zero-shot scoring the abstracts of 51 information science research reports on the UK REF scale correlated with the author's own scores more than any prior method (Spearman's r = 0.68 vs. ChatGPT-4 on full PDFs = 0.51).
42: GPT-4o zero-shot finding the planted limitation in 1,000 perturbed versions of 500 NLP research reports on the novel LIMITGEN-Syn benchmark caught it 52% of the time, below the bespoke multi-agent MARG (68%) and human experts (86%).
43: GPT-4o-mini zero-shot checking 50 RCT research reports from the CONSORT-TM corpus against the reporting guideline CONSORT beat the prior state of the art (F1 score = 0.85 vs. 0.51), though GPT-4-turbo scored higher (0.89).
46: Pairing a human rater with Claude 2 to appraise 112 pediatric surgery systematic reviews with the reporting guideline PRISMA beat the human alone and 5 LLMs combined (Cohen's kappa = 0.92 vs. 0.81 and 0.77), deferring 35% of ratings.
47: Pairing a human rater with GPT 3.5 to appraise 112 pediatric surgery systematic reviews with the critical appraisal tool AMSTAR beat the human alone and 5 LLMs combined (Cohen's kappa = 0.93 vs. 0.80 and 0.82), deferring 52% of ratings.
48: Pairing a human rater with Claude 3 Opus to appraise 56 RCTs from the database PragMeta with the applicability tool PRECIS-2 agreed more than the human alone and 5 LLMs combined (weighted kappa = 0.73 vs. 0.57 and 0.49), deferring 75%.
49: The bespoke Idea Novelty Checker (GPT-4o, 15-shot with retrieved papers) classifying 32 scientific ideas as novel or not agreed with expert labels more than zero-shot GPT-4o or prompt optimizer TextGRAD (F1 score = 0.79 vs. 0.65 and 0.76).
80: Swapping the facet-based reranker in the bespoke Idea Novelty Checker (o3-mini, GPT-4o reranking) for a general-relevance one cut its accuracy at flagging 58 not-novel scientific ideas from 89.7% to 13.8%.
81: Removing the knowledge-guided module from the bespoke Ours-SciBERT, which fuses human and ChatGPT knowledge to predict the novelty of ICLR 2022 research reports' methods, dropped it to its SciBERT backbone's level (F1 score = 0.83 vs. 0.73).
82: Poe Assistant, GPT 3.5, and Google Bard acting as IRB members on 10 health research ethics case studies answered all 10, yet compared to a handbook's answers at least one missed issues in 9 domains and all missed post-trial access.
